topics.title: Tourette’s and a Radio Interview
topics.summary: During an interview, a man with Tourettes Syndrome discusses his discharge from Cassell Associates due to disruptive behavior stemming from his condition. He struggles with involuntary vocalizations and movements while explaining the neurological disorder's impact on his work life, leading to further questions about its causes.

topics.title: The Abdominizer Debate and Channel 9 Concerns
topics.summary: Howard discusses the effectiveness of ‘the abdominizer,’ a sit-up device, debating with Doug who claims it was once sold for $50. The conversation shifts to concerns about Channel 9’s production quality and financial stability, with callers expressing frustration over its lack of innovation and control.

topics.title: Radio Host Rant and CD Obsession
topics.summary: A radio host rages against a syndicated talk show personality, dismissing him as ‘the grease man’ while obsessing over a new CD package featuring himself. He details its potential Grammy nominations and meticulously describes the contents, frequently interrupting with insults directed at other figures in media.

topics.title: Letterman Escapes Connecticut Hospital
topics.summary: During a radio segment, callers discuss Mrs. David Letterman’s voluntary departure from a Connecticut hospital following an incident involving a laughing police officer. The conversation centers on the circumstances of her leaving and speculation about whether it constituted a crime.

topics.title: Erra’s Wild Money Plans
topics.summary: During a chaotic phone-in, Erra reveals his plans to buy pigs and a Gigantor boombox with $16.3 million, attempt to acquire Tyne Daly's home number, invest in Shea Stadium via an umbrella, and express frustration about opportunities for Black Americans.

topics.title: Cave Rescue & Monkey Heads
topics.summary: During the broadcast, a woman named Emily Moblin was rescued from Carlsbad Caverns after falling into a deep cave while mapping it; simultaneously, reports surfaced about stolen skulls – including those intended for medical school - being found in New York City and subsequently recovered by police. Howard discusses phone calls and his wife's opinions.

topics.title: Teenage Suicide Debate and Captive Release
topics.summary: The broadcast features a discussion about teenage suicide rates and proposed government funding for programs to address them. Congressman Gary Ackerman argues against pouring more money into the problem, suggesting troubled family environments are the root cause. Following this is an interview with Roger Cooper, recently released after years of captivity in Iran, who expresses shock at his freedom.

topics.title: Prison Release & Radio Mishaps
topics.summary: A recently released prisoner expresses relief at his freedom while making awkward comments about a co-host, followed by reports on Iranian hostage releases and restrictive abortion legislation in North Dakota. The broadcast concludes with an accidental nose pick and a bizarre discussion regarding ten children.
